nina: Quick note - sample edge app failing after bundling with different bundlers. Repro below.

nina: Symptom: built worker shows `ReferenceError: require is not defined` or import/export mismatch depending on bundler.

omar: Repro steps: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-edge-sdk-quick && npm ci && npm run build:vite && npx miniflare dist/worker.js -> fails. Rollup SSR shows "does not provide an export named 'default'".

tara: Root cause hypothesis: package entry selection + CJS interop helpers leaking into ESM output. Our published SDK has main/module but no conditional exports, and TypeScript/rollup config sometimes leaves `require()` calls.

nina: Minimal handler: `import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; export default async () => new Response((await Redwood.generate({prompt:'hi'})).text);` Post-build some chunks contain `require('crypto')`.

omar: Temporary dev workaround: alias the ESM entry in vite.config: `alias: {'@redwood-inference/sdk':'/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js'}`. Confirms entry selection.

tara: Recommended fixes: add conditional "exports" with import/require, publish clean dist/esm (no CJS wrappers) and dist/cjs, add a bundler smoke matrix in CI (vite/webpack/rollup + miniflare), and add a release check to grep for `require(` in ESM artifacts.

ci-bot: CI failure: sdk-edge-smoke job 1748888800 -> ReferenceError: require is not defined.

nina: Omar will open a small PR for exports + smoke CI. Tara will clean the ESM build pipeline. Will post a short support note with workaround.

omar: picking this up now, will include grep guard in release job.
